subject: chemistry

hotspots.label: The balanced equation
hotspots.description: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O — every atom on the left is matched on the right. This equation obeys conservation of mass.
hotspots.positionHint: The full equation scene with its molecule rows.
hotspots.function: Shows a fully balanced chemical equation.

hotspots.label: Matched atom counts
hotspots.description: The count layer splits every molecule into atoms — 4 hydrogens and 2 oxygens on each side, perfectly matched.
hotspots.positionHint: The split-out atoms with matching tallies on each side.
hotspots.function: Shows the equal atom counts that make it balanced.

hotspots.label: Coefficients at work
hotspots.description: The coefficients — the 2s in front of H₂ and H₂O — are what make both sides match. Adjusting them is how you balance.
hotspots.positionHint: The highlighted coefficient numbers in front of the formulas.
hotspots.function: Shows the coefficients that balance the equation.

visualStyleNotes: Chemistry palette, Anatomy Atelier bar: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no props. The equation 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O floats centered with molecule rows beneath, lit with soft neutral studio light — no rim-light glow, no bloom, no emissive anywhere. Clean stylized product-render look, specimen-quality not cartoon. Formula tiles: soft off-white with app-rendered glyphs; molecule rows: ball-stick in CPK colors (hydrogen warm off-white, oxygen muted red). Strong saturated color is reserved for the small flat hotspot dots and the coefficient highlights (amber / molecular-green / coral accents from the Chemistry palette). Slow auto-rotation, calm, minimal chrome.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0 everywhere, single 2K shared texture atlas. Formula tiles: soft off-white matte, roughness ~0.6. Molecule spheres: CPK colors, roughness ~0.45-0.5. Bond rods: thin graphite cylinders. No emissive channels anywhere — any glow is handled by app runtime UI.
assetBrief:
SUBJECT: the balanced equation 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, built to be read as 'equal atoms on both sides — the true recipe.' Three procedural layers, all clean primitives:

1) MAIN: a flat equation scene — formula tiles (app-rendered glyphs) `2H₂` + `O₂` on the left, an arrow tile, `2H₂O` on the right; beneath, molecule rows: left shows two H₂ ball-sticks and one O₂, right shows two water ball-sticks. Coefficients subtly highlighted.

2) ATOM COUNT (toggleable layer): all molecules split into atoms that arrange in two matching columns (left and right); the app renders running tallies that end equal (H:4, O:2 both sides) with a soft balance confirmation glow.

3) UNBALANCE DEMO (toggleable layer): the coefficient on 2H₂O dims to 1 (making H₂ + O₂ → H₂O), the right-side oxygen count drops to 1, and the tally shows a mismatch — a red 'unbalanced' hint (app-rendered) appears. The atoms visibly do not match.

Camera: framed so the full equation and molecule rows fit with negative space; auto-rotate default. Budget 8-12k triangles. Named nodes: Tile_2H2, Tile_O2, Tile_H2O, EquationArrow, Molecules_Reactants, Molecules_Products, AtomColumns, Tallies, BalanceGlow. All labels are hotspot dots in the app layer.
